sections.title: Names, spelling, and pronouns
body: Ask Hur stavar du det? when a name is unfamiliar. Answer Det stavas …
Å, ä and ö are separate letters at the end of the Swedish alphabet.
Keep every person's real name spelling; do not make it look Swedish.

examples.en: How do you spell the surname?

sections.title: Pronouns and spelling
body: Subject pronouns are jag, du, han, hon, den, det, vi, ni and de.
Use Vad heter du? with a classmate. Vad heter ni? may be polite, though du is common in modern Swedish.
Written jag may sound like ja; written de is normally pronounced dom. Keep standard spelling.

assignment.title: Episode 2 mission: Names, spelling, and pronouns
assignment.instructions:
LISTEN: Hear the audio twice and answer: Which spelling is correct?

READ: Read once for purpose and once for detail. Answer: What is Nora's surname?

SPEAK: Ask a name and its spelling, then spell yours. Try once without the model, then repeat more clearly.

WRITE: Fill a simple form with a fictional first name and surname. Check word order and spelling.

TRANSFER: Repeat at reception using ni once.

RETURN: Ask Vad heter du? and spell your name.
assignment.model:
Speaking: Vad heter du? Jag heter Noor. Det stavas N-O-O-R.
Writing: Förnamn: Noor
Efternamn: Ali

takeaways: Rule: Subject pronouns are jag, du, han, hon, den, det, vi, ni and de.
Return: Ask Vad heter du? and spell your name.
